problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨2\operatorname{cot}⁡(2\pi t),\,{sin}^{2}⁡(2\pi t)⟩,\,0<t<\frac{1}{4}.
$$

Calculate the components of the velocity vector $v$ at time $t=\frac{1}{8}.$ Do not round the answers.

$v(\frac{1}{8})=⟨${{field-1}},
{{field-2}}$⟩$
worked_solution:
The particle's velocity vector is given by the derivative of its position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cot}⁡(2\pi t)),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({sin}^{2}⁡(2\pi t))⟩ \\  & =⟨-4\pi {csc}^{2}⁡(2\pi t),4\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi t)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi t)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the velocity when $t=\frac{1}{8},$ we substitute into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\frac{1}{8}) & =⟨-4\pi {csc}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}),4\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})⟩ \\  & =⟨-4\pi (\sqrt{2})^{2},4\pi (\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}})(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}})⟩ \\  & =⟨-4\pi (2),4\pi (\frac{1}{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-8\pi ,\,2\pi ⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
